text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Israel lodged a complaint with the five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in south Lebanon a day after a Katyusha rocket hit north Israel.
-Prime Minister Hariri said "we are working to control the escalated tension in the south".
-The Lebanese-Syrian High Coordination committee will hold an extraordinary meeting in Damascus on Saturday on bilateral economic relations.
-Israel's coordinator for Lebanon Lubrani blames Lebanese government for tension on the Lebanese Israeli borders.
-President Hrawi fears Israeli military operations to displace southern villagers.
-Parliament Speaker Berri blames PM Hariri for crisis between cabinet and army over army officer's promotion.
-Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer said its purchase of Paris-based Banque Banorabe-France cost an estimated $53 million.
-Foriegn Minister Bouez said Lebanon may file a complaint to the U.N. Security Council if tension in the south continues.
